predecessors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
predecessors.text: the Kashmir Valley, annexed by the Company 'as war indemnity, on 9 March 1846' and sold on 16 March

predecessors.name: Sikh Empire
predecessors.text: Jammu, Ladakh and Baltistan, which Gulab Singh's Dogras held under Sikh suzerainty

successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: the part of the state that stayed with India after the ceasefire of 1 January 1949, with Ladakh

successors.name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
successors.text: Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, 'one-third of the state'

ledger.x: 1858: the state passes under the paramountcy of the Crown.
1891: Hunza and Nagar come under Kashmir's suzerainty.
26 March 1935: the British lease the Gilgit wazarat west of the Indus.
15 August 1947: British suzerainty over the state ends.
November 1947: the western districts pass to Pakistan.
1947: Hunza and Nagar accede to Pakistan.
14 August 1948: Skardu falls and Baltistan passes to Pakistan.
1 January 1949: the ceasefire divides the state.

wars.name: Dogra-Yasin struggle for Gilgit
wars.outcome: Gohar Aman took Gilgit from the Dogras in 1852; he ruled until 1860, and 'Shortly after his death Dogras recaptured Gilgit from his son' (Gohar Aman page; Gilgit-Baltistan page: 'It was not until his death in 1860 that Dogras finally managed to subdue…

wars.name: Hunza-Nagar Campaign
wars.outcome: Hunza and Nagar 'again subjugated by Anglo-Dogra forces in 1891'.

wars.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1947-1948
wars.outcome: Accession to India on 26 October 1947; Gilgit mutiny on 1 November; Mirpur taken on 25 November 1947; ceasefire at 23.59 hrs on 1 January 1949 with Pakistan holding one-third of the state.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Amritsar draws the state as the hill country between the Indus and the Ravi, and Captain Abbott's 1847 commission fixed only the line west of the Jhelum and along the Kishanganga; the Karakoram, Aksai Chin and Chinese…
